name: FP-1 / FP-2

placement_rationale.text: 308 km reflects FP-1/FP-2's confirmed strike depth into Russian territory as a one-way-attack airframe, not a launch-site offset from the line — like the rest of Ukraine's deep-strike drone family, the launch point itself sits inside Ukraine. This asset's own characteristics note the Starlink-relayed terminal-guidance link but don't record a single flight-range figure, so 308 km is read against doctrine.md §2's 10–150+ km medium/long-range strike layer extended into the strategic_rear band, consistent with how the sibling Beaver/Scythe/Lyutyy entries in this same category are placed rather than against the highest ranges reported for this airframe elsewhere.

characteristics: 40kg blast-fragmentation warhead (25kg tetryl HE + 15kg steel balls)
Starlink (or equivalent satellite) link enabling FPV control during terminal approach
Strength: Satellite-relayed terminal guidance gives precision approach unusual among long-range OWA-UAVs, most of which fly pre-programmed routes with no terminal correction
Limitation: Reliance on satellite comms for terminal guidance is itself a dependency that could be targeted by counter-satellite-communications EW if that capability matures
Estimated quantity available: Major, ongoing production; exact numbers not disclosed
employment_notes: Became one of the 'household name' assets of Ukraine's strategic strike campaign; the Starlink-guided terminal phase is a direct extension of the same satellite-comms dependency pattern documented across FPV and reconnaissance drones
contrast_vs_traditional: Like the Beaver, FP-1/FP-2 push the deep-strike layer doctrine.md describes running from 10 to 150+ km out past its traditional bounds — a role that used to require a cruise missile or a manned strike sortie now costs a small fraction of either, changing what a defender has to budget for rather than just what it has to intercept.
